classification.difficultyReason: Identify extreme angles by opposite side length and link the two specified rules.

content.prompt: Consider the triangle shown. Answer to the nearest degree.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use cosine rule to find the size of the largest angle.

spec.description: Schematic closed triangle with horizontal base, apex above, dark-blue edges and black exterior side labels. Preserve the source's acute-looking apex despite the numerical lengths implying an obtuse angle. No visible vertex names, angle marks or angle labels.
spec.mathematics: Left slope 12; right slope 13; base 20. Largest angle opposite 20; smallest angle opposite 12. Drawing intentionally not to scale.

answer.worked:
The largest angle $A$ is opposite side $20$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos A&=\frac{12^2+13^2-20^2}{2(12)(13)}\\[8pt]A&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{87}{312}\right)\\[8pt]A&\approx106^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use sine rule to find the size of the smallest angle.

answer.worked:
The smallest angle $B$ is opposite side $12$. Use the unrounded value of $A$ from part a.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin B}{12}&=\frac{\sin A}{20}\\[8pt]B&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{12\sin A}{20}\right)\\[8pt]B&\approx35^\circ\end{align*}$$
